subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: ADV carries acceptance-criterion content in THREE parallel representations today, all keyed off ContractItem.text: (1) the canonical typed ContractItem.text (warrant-stripped at mint), (2) the legacy state.acceptanceCriteria string[] projection (re-derived on every contractSet), and (3) the AcceptanceCriteriaSetSignal criteria string[]. Eight consumer surfaces read these: parser/mint, schemas, state projections, gate-readiness, briefing packets, review matrix, archive rendering, and the public generated schema. The coherence anchor is a single JSON.stringify drift check (CONTRACT_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA_DRIFT) that compares representation (2) against (1). Gate-readiness, review-matrix validation, required-obligation routing, and archive rendering are all ID/status/flag-based and NEVER read criterion text or variant — they are structurally variant-agnostic. The text-reading consumers (drift check, acceptanceCriteriaFromContract, briefing contract section, projectContractCoverage) are the coherence-critical set: any structured variant must keep .text as the single canonical serialization so these stay coherent. The existing warrant mechanism (parseWarrantTag -> typed warrants:string[] annotation parsed once at mint, text stays canonical, renderers optionally surface it) is the proven pattern to mirror.

validation.notes: No blockers to the research objective. All 8 consumer surfaces mapped with evidence; 2 concrete edge cases + 1 replay/compat edge case identified; recommendation is evidence-backed. The proposal's discovery agenda item 5 (deterministic validation vs advisory linting) is answered by evidence — the implementation-free guard has NO code implementation today (spec/command prose only), and spec-ambiguity.ts already treats GWT as advisory prose. Promoting structured-criterion syntax to gate authority would contradict the proposal's own 'Must not represent syntax validity as behavioral proof' constraint.

tradeoffs: Typed-additive variant parsed once at mint adds a schema field + parser branch + regenerates public change.schema.json (additive-optional = safe, but widens the public contract surface external consumers must tolerate).

Keeping text canonical preserves the 3-representation coherence and the drift check, but means renderers that want structured display (Given/When/Then) must re-derive or carry the typed variant alongside text — a small dual-source risk bounded by single-mint-parse.

Gate-readiness/review-matrix/archive are variant-agnostic today, so the change can land without touching them — but a future variant-driven evidence-policy derivation (e.g. scenario->test, evidence->artifact_reference) WOULD enter the gate path and must stay consistent with the existing section->policy mapping.

A pure rendered-only approach (parse GWT from text at each read) avoids the schema/parser change but creates N re-parsers (drift check, briefing, archive, projection) that can diverge — exactly the anti-pattern CONTRACT_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA_DRIFT exists to prevent.

alternatives_considered.option: Typed-additive optional variant field mirroring the warrant mechanism (parse once at mint, text stays canonical)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Matches the proposal Constraint ('prefer typed, deterministic'), preserves backward compat (version stays 1, optional field is additive-safe for the public schema + Temporal replay), keeps the drift-check/projection coherence intact, and reuses the proven parseWarrantTag -> typed-annotation pattern. Lowest-risk way to get a single parse source of truth.

alternatives_considered.option: Rendered-only: parse Given/When/Then from free text at each consumer read
alternatives_considered.rationale: Violates P33 (structural-correctness) and the existing drift-check design: N independent re-parsers of .text can diverge, and the JSON.stringify drift comparison would become order/whitespace-fragile across renderers. Also fails the proposal's 'prefer typed over free-text convention' constraint.

alternatives_considered.option: Discriminated union replacing text with structured scenario/evidence/spec_law/constraint objects + version:2
alternatives_considered.rationale: Breaking migration across every persisted change (public change.schema.json $id, ChangeContractSchema.version=z.literal(1), dual-write projection, poisoned-history recovery all assume the current shape). Disproportionate to the readability goal and violates the backward-compat constraint.

alternatives_considered.option: Promote implementation-free/structured-syntax validity to a hard gate blocker
alternatives_considered.rationale: Contradicts the proposal 'Must not represent syntax validity as behavioral proof'. The discovery guard is already spec'd advisory-only and has no code; spec-ambiguity.ts treats GWT as advisory remediation. Keep advisory.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed with a TYPED, ADDITIVE, OPTIONAL variant annotation on ContractItem parsed once at mint, with text remaining the canonical serialization. Mirror the existing warrant mechanism (parseWarrantTag -> typed warrants:string[]): add e.g. variant?: {kind:'scenario'|'evidence'|'spec_law'|'constraint'; ...} parsed in buildContractFromAgreement alongside parseWarrantTag, so all three text-based representations (ContractItem.text, state.acceptanceCriteria, drift check) stay coherent without changes. Gate-readiness/review-matrix/archive need no change (they are id/status-based). Briefing packet contract section gets the variant as an additional optional surface field. Regenerate change.schema.json (additive-optional = safe). Keep the implementation-free guard advisory (no gate authority). Before design, resolve: (a) exact variant discriminator + required-vs-advisory fields per variant, (b) whether variant can drive evidencePolicy derivation (today it is section-heading-derived — a variant-driven override would enter the gate path and needs its own coherence story), and (c) warrant-tag placement when a variant needs a warrant in a non-trailing sub-field (parseWarrantTag only handles trailing tag today).

subagent_reports.recommendation: Map is complete and evidence-backed. Recommend the design phase adopt: (1) typed-additive optional variant on ContractItem mirroring the warrant mechanism; (2) text stays canonical so the drift check + acceptanceCriteriaFromContract + briefing/archive projections stay coherent; (3) regenerate the public change.schema.json; (4) keep implementation-free/structured-syntax as advisory, not gate authority. The two hard constraints forcing this shape are ChangeContractSchema.version=z.literal(1) + the published change.schema.json $id (no breaking migration) and the 3-representation coherence anchored by CONTRACT_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA_DRIFT.
follow_ups: Design phase must specify the variant discriminator and which fields are required vs advisory per variant (discovery agenda item 1).

Design must decide whether a variant may override the section-heading-derived evidencePolicy; if yes, gate-readiness (checkUnresolvedVerificationEvidence, isProofBearingEvidencePolicy) and the review-matrix evidencePolicy field become variant-aware and need coherence tests.

The design's additive optional-variant approach is structurally well-fit to the existing code, not a new subsystem. Five leverage candidates found; four shrink the task surface by reusing proven structure, one localizes rendering. No correctness blocker. [1] ADOPT_NOW — Atomic mint already satisfies AC5; no new rollback design needed. buildContractFromAgreement validates via ChangeContractSchema.parse() as its final step and the tool layer persists only on success; all CONTRACT_* errors throw before return, so a malformed (Zod-invalid) variant cannot replace a stored contract. payoff:high risk:low tie:AC5,C3 evidence:contract-mint.ts:198,214,237,242 prior:new.

The same extract-before-persist step that strips [warrant: ...] (contract-mint.ts:189-192) can parse+strip a variant tag, keeping exactly one structural interpretation path and preserving canonical text — directly realizing the design's anti-parallel-interpretation rejection rationale. payoff:high risk:low tie:AC1,AC4,C1,C3,DONT2 evidence:warrant.ts:53-89 + contract-mint.ts:187-192 prior:new.

[3] ADOPT_NOW — Additive variant field is a one-line .optional() change following established precedent (sourceHash/notRequiredReason/requiredCritical/warrants are all optional; warrants added identically by addAcWarrantGuard). [4] DESIGN_AROUND — Coverage, review-matrix, and drift enforcement are structurally variant-blind (keyed on item.id / kind===acceptance_criterion / text). Variant therefore needs ZERO awareness in those code paths for AC7 to hold, but this must be encoded as an explicit design invariant with a regression test so a future variant-aware feature cannot silently regress it. payoff:medium risk:low tie:AC7,OOS2 evidence:contract.ts:101-109,186-225,227-241 prior:new.

[5] ADOPT_NOW — Agent-facing contract rendering localizes to one pure surface: buildContractSection maps items to {id,kind,text,status}. Confirming enforcement checks are variant-blind shrinks the task list (good) but must be locked as an explicit invariant/test or a future variant-aware feature could silently regress AC7.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Existing pattern: ChangeContract is a typed spine (rq-contractTrace01); contract.items carry id/kind/text/evidencePolicy/warrants. Legacy acceptanceCriteria is a pure item.text projection (change-state.ts:1250). Warrants are stripped+validated structurally at mint (rq-acWarrant01); malformed warrants throw, never silently drop (satisfies C3). The mint tool path is reject-before-replace: buildContractFromAgreement runs before any signal/state mutation and an outer catch returns an error leaving prior state intact (AC5). Public schemas are generated from Zod via z.toJSONSchema, so optional fields are additive by construction (AC8). Reference pattern for an additive optional annotation is exactly what the design proposes: extend ContractItemSchema with an optional variant field, keep text canonical, parse once at mint, render additive. Deviation from the boring/reference approach: NONE on the core decision. Two implementation-decision gaps remain unpinned (see validation.notes): (GAP-A) canonical-text shape for multi-clause behavioral variants - the line-based mint parser at contract-mint.ts:168,136 cannot ingest multi-line Given/When/Then today, so the design's parse-safe grammar must define whether canonical text is flattened-single-line or preserved-multi-line, AND must state the legacy acceptanceCriteria projection stays item.text-only for variant items; (GAP-B) the DDC2 import-boundary invariant (warrant-boundary.test.ts) on contract-mint.ts/warrant.ts is not named in the design though both files are listed as affected. Neither gap is a contract compromise - both have existing structural guardrails (tests + parser evidence). Spec-law consistency: rq-contractTrace01 (contract.items as source of truth; legacy acceptanceCriteria as projection of AC items) is preserved by the text-canonical decision - variant is presentation metadata, not a new obligation source. rq-acWarrant01 (structural mint-time warrant validation; CONTRACT_UNRESOLVED_WARRANT fails with no contract persisted) is preserved by the commitment to retain bracketed warrant extraction identically for flat and structured input. The agreement Draft Spec Deltas to advance-workflow and adv-discover add new requirements governing variant annotation/authoring and do not weaken existing contract-traceability or warrant law. Nuance to codify in the new spec law: variant syntax must not be treated as behavioral proof (C2) and must not grant acceptance authority (design: Variants affect presentation, not acceptance authority) - these should appear as explicit Given/When/Then scenarios in the added advance-workflow requirement. required_validation_consistency: partial - the design's Design-Derived Criteria align with AC1-AC8 and constraints, but GAP-A and GAP-B leave two invariants implicit that should be pinned before planning.

validation.notes: Design is structurally consistent with AC1-AC8, constraints C1-C3, avoidances DONT1-DONT3, and spec law (rq-contractTrace01, rq-acWarrant01). AC1/AC3/AC5/AC7/AC8 are structurally guaranteed by existing code (additive Zod optionality, text-only legacy projection at change-state.ts:1250, reject-before-replace mint path at tools/contract.ts:325-454, id/evidence-policy-keyed review at gate-readiness.ts:955). AC2/AC6 are sound design invariants (single-parse-at-mint, variant-as-presentation-not-authority) the implementation must enforce. Two non-blocker design gaps to pin before planning (no contract compromise, both have structural guardrails). GAP-A (canonical-text shape for multi-clause variants): the design says text remains canonical and the parse-safe grammar rejects unsupported multi-line forms, but does not state whether canonical text for a behavioral variant is flattened-single-line or preserved-multi-line. This matters because text is consumed by the line-based mint parser (contract-mint.ts:168,136), the legacy acceptanceCriteria projection (change-state.ts:1250), drift checks (contract.ts:107,231), gate-readiness rendering (gate-readiness.ts:955), and the briefing renderer (briefing-packet-renderer.ts:50). Recommend pinning: (a) text shape, (b) explicit invariant that the legacy acceptanceCriteria projection remains item.text-only for variant items (no parallel representation, protects AC6). GAP-B (DDC2 boundary): warrant-boundary.test.ts forbids static tool-registry/tools/* imports in contract-mint.ts and warrant.ts. Any variant-specific validation needing live tool/spec surfaces MUST be injected (as warrantLookup is today), not statically imported. Design should name this invariant in Affected Components/Risks.

tradeoffs: Additive optional annotation preserves backward compatibility (AC3/AC8) at the cost of a second parsed structure that must be kept consistent with canonical text (single-parse invariant, AC6).

Mint-boundary parsing centralizes interpretation (good for warrant/authority safety) but requires extending a line-based parser that today cannot ingest multi-line Given/When/Then blocks (real implementation risk, named in design Risks).
Variants-as-presentation keeps gate-readiness/review-matrix variant-agnostic (AC7) but means reviewers must trust the renderer to surface variant fields faithfully alongside canonical text (AC6).

alternatives_considered.rationale: Breaking migration for every existing ChangeContract; violates rq-contractTrace01 compatibility and AC3/AC8. Optional additive field is strictly simpler. Design rejects this; concur.

documents.proposal:
# Add Structured Acceptance Criteria

## Why

ADV acceptance criteria can be specific yet inconsistently shaped and cognitively dense when a reviewer evaluates a full set. The current model must retain its traceability and verification guarantees while making value, behavior, evidence, and policy obligations easier for people and agents to scan consistently.

## What Changes

Establish a contract-safe structured acceptance-criteria style and supporting ADV behavior for four criterion variants:

- behavioral scenario
- evidence obligation
- spec-law reconciliation
- operational constraint

Success criteria may express an intended beneficiary, outcome, and value. Behavioral criteria may use Gherkin-inspired Given/When/Then/And language where it improves clarity. The resulting format remains compatible with stable contract IDs, typed evidence policies, bracketed warrants, task contract references, and review-matrix evidence.

## User Outcomes

- Reviewers can scan a full contract and quickly distinguish required behavior, evidence, policy reconciliation, and constraints.
- Agents receive a consistent statement of preconditions, triggering context, required outcome, boundaries, and proof route.
- Contributors can understand why a success criterion matters without losing its observable outcome.
- Existing contracts remain trustworthy: criterion identity, warranted capability claims, and verification traceability are preserved.

## Affected Code

Likely areas: contract schemas and parsing, contract validation, discovery and review command guidance, briefing/rendering surfaces, gate-readiness projections, public generated schemas, and their tests.

## Related Repositories

Current Advance repository only. No cross-repository product scope is known.

## Constraints

- Preserve implementation-free, behavioral acceptance intent.
- Preserve `ACn`/`SCn` identity, bracketed warrant semantics, evidence policies, task references, and review-matrix coverage.
- Maintain backward compatibility for existing agreement and contract artifacts.
- Prefer typed, deterministic representation and validation over free-text convention alone.

## Impact

This may affect proposal/discovery authoring, agreement minting, agent briefing, acceptance review, public schemas, and persisted acceptance snapshots. Existing active changes must continue to read and validate without manual rewriting.

## Failure Handling

Malformed or unsupported structured criterion input must produce a clear validation outcome and must not silently discard a warrant, weaken evidence requirements, or partially overwrite an existing contract. Existing compatible contracts remain readable and unchanged on a rejected update.

## Context

Independent format comparison found that raw Cucumber-style syntax is not currently consumed by ADV's contract machinery. In particular, current label and warrant parsing rely on `ACn:`-shaped labels and `[warrant: ...]` tags. The change should capture the readability benefit of structured language without bypassing those structural guarantees.

## Scope

### In Scope

- A canonical, readable structure for success criteria and the four acceptance-criterion variants.
- Contract-safe parsing, representation, validation, rendering, and agent guidance needed to make that structure reliable.
- Compatibility behavior for existing unstructured criteria.

### Out of Scope

- Replacing or integrating the test framework with Cucumber.
- Requiring every criterion to be a behavioral scenario.
- Rewriting unrelated active changes solely to adopt the new style.

### Must Not

# Agreement — Add Structured Acceptance Criteria

## Objectives

- Make full acceptance contracts consistently scannable for reviewers and agents.
- Preserve precise behavioral, evidence, spec-law, and constraint obligations.
- Keep current contract identity, warrant verification, evidence policies, task traceability, and legacy compatibility intact.
- Use structured language to clarify obligations without treating syntax as behavioral proof.

## Success Criteria

- SC1: For reviewers, I need contract items presented by purpose and outcome, so that full-set review is faster and more reliable.
- SC2: For ADV agents, I need each criterion’s context, required result, boundary, and proof route to be unambiguous, so that implementation and review stay aligned.
- SC3: For maintainers, I need existing acceptance contracts to remain readable and traceable, so that structured criteria do not disrupt active or historical work.
- SC4: For release and review workflows, I need warrants, evidence policies, and contract coverage preserved, so that readability does not weaken enforcement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Given an approved criterion classified as behavioral, evidence, spec-law, or constraint, when its agreement is minted, then the contract preserves a typed optional variant annotation while retaining canonical text and stable contract ID.
- AC2: Given a behavioral criterion uses structured language, when it is rendered for review or an agent briefing, then its context, trigger, required outcome, and follow-on boundaries are visibly distinguishable.
- AC3: Given an existing flat-text contract, when it is read, rendered, or reviewed after the change, then it remains usable without manual rewrite and preserves its current effective contract content.
- AC4: Given a criterion contains a valid bracketed warrant, when it is minted or represented in a structured variant, then its warrant is retained and validated through the current structural path. [warrant: tool:adv_contract_mint]
- AC5: Given structured input is malformed or unsupported, when minting or updating is attempted, then ADV returns a clear validation result and leaves the previously valid contract unchanged.
- AC6: Given a structured criterion is included in an agent briefing or reviewer-facing contract view, when the item is rendered, then its variant and canonical obligation are both visible without inventing a second authoritative representation.
- AC7: Given criteria use any supported variant, when task coverage and review-matrix completeness are evaluated, then existing ID-based traceability and evidence-policy behavior remain unchanged.
- AC8: Given the public change schema is generated after the change, when legacy contract data is validated, then existing valid contracts remain schema-compatible.

## Constraints

- C1: The variant annotation is additive and canonical text remains the compatibility anchor.
- C2: Syntax validity must not be treated as behavioral proof.
- C3: Structured input validation must not silently discard warrants, weaken evidence requirements, or partially overwrite an existing valid contract.

## Avoidances

- DONT1: Do not add Cucumber, step definitions, or a test-framework dependency.
- DONT2: Do not silently strip or bypass warrants, evidence obligations, or contract IDs.
- DONT3: Do not require every criterion to use a behavioral scenario variant.

## Out of Scope

- OOS1: Do not bulk-rewrite unrelated active changes solely to adopt the new style.
- OOS2: Do not replace existing task traceability, review-matrix, or acceptance-gate mechanisms.

## Design Questions

- Choose a parse-safe input and rendering form for variant annotations.
- Define advisory versus required variant fields by contract rigor.
- Decide whether variant annotations are persisted in acceptance snapshots or derived for display.

## Discovery Findings

- Current one-line obligation parsing cannot safely consume multi-line Given/When/Then blocks.
- Bracketed warrants are structural input and must remain intact.
- ID-based gate and review-matrix checks can remain variant-agnostic when canonical text stays authoritative.

## Draft Spec Deltas

- `advance-workflow`: add contract-variant and compatibility obligations, including a Given/When/Then scenario for typed additive representation.
- `adv-discover`: add structured-criterion authoring and agreement checkpoint obligations, including a Given/When/Then scenario for preserving warrants and implementation-free intent.

# Design — Add Structured Acceptance Criteria

## Architecture Overview

Extend the existing ChangeContract with an additive optional criterion-variant annotation. Canonical `ContractItem.text` remains the single, flattened one-line obligation string used by legacy projections, drift checks, task traceability, and review-matrix coverage. The annotation carries a variant kind and mint-derived display parts for behavioral scenario, evidence obligation, spec-law reconciliation, or operational constraint; those parts are never independently authored or inferred by downstream renderers.

The agreement-to-contract mint boundary parses approved input once, validates it, normalizes canonical text, and persists both text and typed annotation atomically. Briefing and reviewer renderers consume the annotation to display a consistent review shape. Gate-readiness and review-matrix logic remain ID- and evidence-policy-based.

## Key Decisions

### Additive typed annotation; canonical text remains authoritative

Use an optional typed variant field rather than a new discriminated contract-item union or renderer-only inference.

- **Why:** preserves compatibility with existing `ContractItem.text` consumers and public schema data while making presentation deterministic.
- **Lever citations:** `validator/contract-mint.ts` parses agreement obligations and persists contract items; `temporal/change-state.ts` derives the legacy acceptance-criteria projection from contract item text; `validator/contract.ts` compares that projection for drift; `utils/briefing-packet-renderer.ts` emits contract items to agents.
- **Alternative rejected:** free-text Gherkin blocks or renderer heuristics create parallel interpretation paths and would lose multi-line clauses in the current one-line mint parser.

### Parse and validate at the mint boundary

Accept only a parse-safe representation defined by the contract grammar. Parse it once during `adv_contract_mint`, retain normalized flattened canonical text, and report typed validation failures before contract replacement.

- **Why:** one structural interpretation protects warrant handling and prevents divergent downstream parsing.
- **Lever citations:** `validator/contract-mint.ts` is the agreement parser and invokes warrant handling; `validator/warrant.ts` recognizes and verifies bracketed warrant tags; the contract-set signal persists the parsed result.
- **Failure semantics:** unsupported/malformed structured input returns a clear failure and does not replace the prior valid contract.
- **Compatibility invariant:** legacy `acceptanceCriteria` continues to project only canonical `item.text`, including for variant-bearing items.

### Variants affect presentation, not acceptance authority

Rendering can show Given/When/Then/And fields for behavioral items and purpose-specific layouts for evidence, spec-law, and constraint items. Variant syntax alone does not satisfy an AC.

- **Why:** existing acceptance authority is the approved contract, task coverage, evidence policy, and review matrix.
- **Lever citations:** `temporal/gate-readiness.ts` evaluates review-matrix coverage and passing status by contract IDs; `validator/contract.ts` projects task coverage and proof checks; `tools/contract.ts` persists review-matrix rows.

### Preserve legacy contracts and schema compatibility

Existing items without an annotation render in the current flat form. New schema fields are optional and generated public schemas update additively.

- **Why:** active and historical contracts must remain readable without migration.
- **Lever citations:** `types/changes.ts` defines `ContractItemSchema`; `schema-registry.ts` generates public JSON schemas; `temporal/change-state.ts` projects existing contract text to legacy acceptance criteria.

### Preserve dynamic import boundaries

Any variant validation that resolves live tool or spec surfaces mirrors the established warrant lookup injection path. It must not add static tool-registry imports to contract-mint or warrant modules.

- **Why:** current DDC2 boundary tests protect workflow-reachable module separation.
- **Lever citations:** `validator/warrant.ts` performs structural warrant validation; `warrant-boundary.test.ts` enforces its import boundary.

## Implementation Strategy

1. Define the optional variant schema and mint-derived display parts, preserving normalized one-line `text` as canonical.
2. Extend agreement parsing and `adv_contract_mint` validation to recognize the approved parse-safe notation, preserve bracketed warrants, and reject incomplete structures before mutation.
3. Thread additive fields through Temporal state, contract set signals, snapshots where audit visibility requires it, and public schema generation.
4. Update briefing and reviewer-facing renderers to display each variant consistently while retaining canonical text and ID.
5. Keep task coverage, evidence-policy checks, drift checks, and review-matrix completeness variant-agnostic; add targeted regressions proving that behavior.
6. Update discovery and review guidance so authors select the appropriate variant instead of forcing every obligation into a scenario.
7. Add compatibility, parser-loss, warrant-preservation, failed-update, renderer, projection, DDC2-boundary, and generated-schema tests.

## Affected Components

- `plugin/src/types/changes.ts` — contract item schema.
- `plugin/src/validator/contract-mint.ts` and `plugin/src/validator/warrant.ts` — parse and warrant-preservation boundary.
- `plugin/src/validator/contract.ts` — legacy projection and drift invariants.
- `plugin/src/temporal/change-state.ts` and contract/signal types — persisted state and compatibility projection.
- `plugin/src/utils/briefing-packet-renderer.ts` and review render paths — agent/reviewer presentation.
- `plugin/src/temporal/gate-readiness.ts` and `plugin/src/tools/contract.ts` — regression-confirmed authority remains unchanged.
- `plugin/src/schema-registry.ts` and generated schema artifacts.
- `plugin/src/validator/warrant-boundary.test.ts` — dynamic import boundary regression coverage.
- Discovery/review command contracts and capability specs.

## LBP Analysis

A typed optional annotation is the smallest long-term structure that gives reviewers consistent formatting without adding Cucumber, step definitions, or a second source of truth. It reuses the established pattern in which agreement text is deterministically parsed into typed contract state and structural metadata such as warrants is retained separately. A renderer-only solution would require repeated inference; a new contract union would impose a breaking migration.

## Design-Derived Criteria

- Variant data is parsed once at mint and is never inferred by a downstream renderer.
- Variant display parts and canonical text are derived atomically from one approved input; canonical text is normalized to a flattened single line.
- A rejected structured update preserves the complete previously valid contract state.
- Warrant extraction and validation remain identical for flat and structured criterion input.
- Existing items without a variant retain their current canonical text and legacy acceptance-criteria projection.
- Generated public schemas remain backward-compatible through additive optional fields.
- Contract-mint and warrant modules retain their dynamic import boundary.

## Risks / Mitigations

- **Parser ambiguity:** define one parse-safe grammar and reject unsupported multi-line continuation forms; cover failure cases.
- **Warrant loss:** retain current bracketed tag extraction as a dedicated regression invariant.
- **Projection drift:** retain flattened canonical text and assert legacy projection equality after mint/update.
- **Historical compatibility:** make all new fields optional and test old serialized contract fixtures.
- **Over-formalization:** preserve non-scenario variants and keep syntax validity advisory rather than acceptance authority.

## Design Leverage Scout

Five candidates considered. Adopted: reuse bracketed-tag extraction at mint; add one optional schema field; rely on existing atomic mint rejection rather than new rollback; extend the single briefing contract mapping. Design around: retain variant-blind coverage, review-matrix, and drift enforcement as an explicit invariant with regressions rather than modifying enforcement code.

## Validator Result

Validator: caution — no blockers. The core additive, parse-once, text-canonical design matches existing contract and warrant law. This record pins the two requested invariants: flattened canonical text remains the only legacy projection source, and variant validation retains the existing dynamic import boundary.
